precepts.text: Woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born. That is what the scripture says about the betrayer.
precepts.point: Apollonius, pretending peace, forbare till the holy day of the Sabbath, and taking the Jews keeping holy day, commanded his men to arm themselves, and slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the Sabbath. But Judas Maccabeus with nine others withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, and fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Jason “received shame for the reward of his treason.” Christ spoke directly about the betrayer: “The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.” Put that with the millstone about the neck, and both mean the same thing for the traitor: go die.

See how all the evil Jason did came back on him. “In the end therefore he had an unhappy return, being accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt.”

“Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians”, that is Sparta, “thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred: And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.”

It had been good for that man if he had not been born. That is what the scripture says about the betrayer, whether it is Jason with Onias, Judas with Christ, or those who betray their brethren in this truth today.

precepts.text: He that loveth gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof. Gold hath been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present. Sometimes money is your ruin: you stop making sound decisions, you are willing to do anything for it. That is why you see these young women degrading themselves on these platforms for money; what morals do you have, and then you go home and kiss your kids? It is a stumblingblock unto them that sacrifice unto it. If money is all you think about and all you talk about, if your existence is based off money, then that is your god; you made a sacrifice to it. But blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and hath not gone after gold. Why? Because it is hard to have riches and keep the commandments; with money you can be enticed so many ways, because you can do whatever you want. But when you are without blemish, you use those finances properly and it does not mess with your head. You have a lot of money, but you have not made it your god.
precepts.point: This man walked with Christ. He saw the healing, he was around the commandment keeping; but that money lust is never enough. He desired money and riches more than anything. And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver. And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him. Ultimately Judas betrayed Lord Jesus Christ.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
Judas asked the chief priests, “What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you?” and “they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.” Sirach shows what that love of money does: “He that loveth gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.”

“Gold hath been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.” Sometimes money is the ruin of you. You stop making sound decisions; you are willing to do anything for it. That is why so many young women today are on OnlyFans and on these podcasts, doing anything they can to make money, willing to get booed on in another country for money. What morals do you have, and then you go home and kiss your kids? It might look good because of the opportunity, but all things ain't good.

“It is a stumblingblock unto them that sacrifice unto it, and every fool shall be taken therewith.” If money is all you think about and all you talk about, if your existence is based off money, money, money, then that is your god. That is why it says you made a sacrifice to it.

“Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and hath not gone after gold.” Why blessed? Because it is hard to have riches and keep the commandments. With money you can be enticed in so many ways; you can buy what you want and do whatever you want, and some feel they are above everybody. But when you are without blemish, you use your finances properly and it don't mess with your head. You have a lot of money, but you ain't made it your god.

Judas walked with Christ. He saw the healing and was around the commandment keeping, but that money lust is never enough, and he desired riches more than anything. Gold was his ruin: money was his demise.

precepts.text: Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your own hands. When you put that sin above everything, that is what you are seeking: death. Money can be your destruction. Women can be your destruction. Food, alcohol, drugs can be your destruction. That is the appetite in us that we constantly want to feed, and we have to stop it.
precepts.point: This man walked with Christ. He saw the healing, he was around the commandment keeping; but that money lust is never enough. He desired money and riches more than anything. And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver. And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him. Ultimately Judas betrayed Lord Jesus Christ.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your hands.” Don't seek death. When you put that sin above everything, that is exactly what you are seeking: death. Judas did it with his own hands when he “sought opportunity to betray him” for thirty pieces of silver, and he destroyed himself.

Money can be your destruction. Women can be your destruction. Food can be your destruction. Alcohol and drugs can be your destruction. These are the appetites in us that we constantly want to feed, and we have to stop it.

This is war, and people will give you up for money. It runs through history: the Black Panther Party, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X. We had a whole Israelite camp back in the day break up because of money, and today certain brothers get pushed on every platform as the face of the Israelites while the bishops and deacons really out here teaching are kept off. If you are weak in spirit, betrayal comes with money.

So be wise. A lot of times we are going to fall, but you don't sit down in a fetal position; you repent and move forward and sin no more. The destruction a man pulls on himself comes from the works of his own hands, and the way out is to stop feeding the appetite before it becomes your demise, like it became Judas'.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
At the Passover dinner Christ took the cup and said, “For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” The blood the Israelites put on the doorposts in ancient Egypt represented Christ's blood. It represented the new covenant: Christ coming and dying for our sins.

John shows who the lamb is: “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God”. Christ is called the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year represents Christ. He is that sacrifice.

So we do not sacrifice anymore, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today; some brothers are crazy. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God. Believing in Christ and doing what is right is what protects you from the wrath of God.

precepts.text: For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. He died for our sins, so you do not have to kill a lamb and put blood over the doorpost so you do not die. You believe in Christ, you keep the commandments, we come together, we break bread and drink wine: you are under the new covenant.
precepts.point: He took the cup, saying, Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. That blood that we used to put on the doorpost represents Christ's blood: it represents the new covenant, Christ coming and dying for our sins. So do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
The bread represents Christ's body, and the cup his blood “shed for many for the remission of sins.” Paul says it plainly: “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

Christ is our passover. The lamb that was killed represents Christ, and that is saying a lot. He was sacrificed for us; he came and died for our sins.

So you do not have to go kill a lamb and put the blood over the doorpost so that you do not die. You believe in Christ and you keep the commandments, and we come together, we break bread and we drink wine, as Christ did with the twelve at the Passover. That is being under the new covenant.

precepts.text: Ye have the poor always with you.
precepts.point: A Hebrew servant goes free in the seventh year and is furnished liberally from the flock, the floor and the winepress.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 15:11 says, “For the poor shall never cease out of the land”, and Christ said the same: “For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.”

Notice what that tells us. In verses 5 and 6 the Lord promised that if we carefully hearken to observe all the commandments, “thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow; and thou shalt reign over many nations, but they shall not reign over thee.” That happened in the time of David and Solomon. There would even be no poor among us. But in verse 11 he says the poor shall never cease out of the land. The Lord was letting us know we were not going to be keeping those commandments too long.

So the command stands: “Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.” If there be a poor man of one of thy brethren, “thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother”, but lend him sufficient for his need. And beware of the wicked thought, “The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand”: imagine it is the sixth year, and you refuse your brother because in twelve months you will not get it back. If he cries unto the Lord against thee, “it be sin unto thee.” Give, and do not be grieved, and the Lord will bless you in all your works.

This is also why the Hebrew servant sold to you, a brother who was poor and lacked food, water and shelter, served only six years and was not sent away empty, but furnished liberally out of the flock, the floor and the winepress, so he or she could have a fresh start and be self-sufficient. It is because we were bondmen in Egypt and the Lord redeemed us. All the laws intertwine with love thy neighbour as thyself.

precepts.text: Ye have the poor always with you; poverty does not cease, so the commandment is to open thine hand to thy poor brother.
precepts.point: The poor shall never cease out of the land; Christ said the same, that the poor are always going to be among us. That is why no campaign can fight poverty out of existence: Christ said it will always be among us.

note.label: Deuteronomy 15: The Year of Release and the Hebrew Servant

precepts.why:
“For the poor shall never cease out of the land”. Christ said the same: “For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.” The poor are always going to be among us; poverty does not cease. That is why no campaign can fight poverty out of existence: Christ said it will always be among us.

Because the poor never cease, the commandment stands: “Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.” Give him surely, and let not thine heart be grieved when thou givest, for because of this thing the Most High shall bless thee in all thy works. Beware of the thought in a wicked heart that the seventh year, the year of release, is at hand, and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother; if he cry unto the Lord against thee, it is sin unto thee.

Notice that Esau had this Bible, these commandments and these laws, yet worked us to death for over four hundred years, and when they released us we did not go out with anything. They had these laws written before them and did not do them.

precepts.text: Christ told His own that one of them, he that dipped in the dish, would betray Him, and it had been good for that man if he had not been born.
precepts.point: This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
Christ was betrayed the same way, by one of his own. “And as they did eat, he said, Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.” They were exceeding sorrowful and every one asked, Lord, is it I? “He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me.” One that ate at his table, a man his acquaintance who walked with him, like the one who reproached David.

“The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.” Judas asked, “Master, is it I? He said unto him, Thou hast said.” It was not an enemy; it was one who took sweet counsel with him.

precepts.text: The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
precepts.point: The formula is given here. The flesh is weak and profits nothing; the spirit is strengthened by the word, and that is how the temptation is endured.

note.label: Matthew 4: The Temptation in the Wilderness and the Calling of the Fishers

precepts.why:
Christ tells his disciples, “Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” The flesh is weak, and that is exactly where the tempter aimed when Christ was an hungred.

The spirit is willing, but it has to be strengthened, and it is strengthened by the word. Christ, weak in the flesh after forty days, stood on “every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God”, and that is how the temptation is endured: watch, pray, and feed the spirit on the word, because the flesh will fail.

precepts.text: They sought false witness, and at the last two came saying, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial. “Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death; But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses, And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.”

They twisted it. He said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”, speaking of the temple of his body; they made it, I am able to destroy the temple of God. They never understood the sign they asked for, and in the end they sought false witness with it to put him to death.

precepts.text: The chief priests, the elders, and all the council sought false witness against Christ to put Him to death.
precepts.point: The same thing was done to Paul in Acts 21, when they charged that he taught the people not to keep the customs of Moses.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
Unable to beat Stephen with the scriptures, they “suborned men”: bribed and induced them to give false testimony that he spoke “blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.” It is the same thing that was done to Christ. “Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death”. When the leaders cannot answer the word, they go looking for false witnesses.

Stephen was not teaching anyone to break the laws. He was teaching them to accept Christ as the sacrifice, and they could not tell the difference between mercy and keeping the law. So what was done to Christ was done to Stephen, and the same thing was done to Paul in Acts 21, when they charged that he taught the people not to keep the customs of Moses.

precepts.text: His blood of the new testament is shed for many for the remission of sins, the many of Israel.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.”

Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under the first covenant. The new testament is the covenant with the house of Israel, and the many are the many of Israel.

So what do they have to watch out for? “Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation:” Watch and pray that you enter not into temptation. You know what is evil for you. Everybody, every man, every woman, once you self-examine you know what your weak zones are, and you pray to the Lord; remember he said lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. “the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” Your spirit could be willing, but the flesh is weak. So this is what you have to watch for.
